text:
The amplifier is a source follower (M1 drain at vdd, source at vout), biased by an NMOS current sink (M2) mirrored from the diode-connected reference M3. The gain of -1.2 dB matches a follower. Its bandwidth is set by gm(M1)/C_L, so the failing f3dB (570 MHz vs 2.2 GHz) and GBW (496 MHz vs 1.9 GHz) imply M1's transconductance is about 4x too low. Power is only 169 µW against a 1.4 mW limit, so the bias current is too low. The most likely culprit is the bias mirror: the M2/M3 width ratio (7.49) sets the sink current, and a wrong reference width or mirror ratio would starve M1. I can't confirm the original sizes from the data alone, so the ranking below is a best estimate.

```json
{"ranking": ["M3", "M2", "M1"], "fault": "Mirror ratio/reference sizing corrupted (likely M3 width reduced, giving M2/M3 ratio ~7.5), so the sink current into the follower is too low; this starves M1's gm and cuts f3dB and GBW well below spec, while power stays far under the limit."}
```
